sources.title: BlockFusion wins approval to reopen bitcoin mine on Frontier Avenue

profile.campus_note: One of 11 buildings OpenStreetMap contributors have mapped under this name in this locality, numbered west to east.
profile.research_note: Session 2026-09-03: local press names the operating entity "Northeast Data LLC" doing business as BlockFusion. All 10 OSM nodes for this name sit within ~250m of each other on the same Frontier Avenue industrial site and resolve to the same address via Nominatim reverse geocode; treated as one multi-building campus, not 10 distinct facilities.

reading.body:
BlockFusion Niagara Falls is a multi-building campus on Frontier Avenue in western New York, currently operating or reopening as a cryptocurrency mining facility according to local press from 2026, with no published power specifications or IT load figures available on the operator's spec page. The site comprises approximately 10 buildings clustered within 250 meters and verified to the same address, but BlockFusion has not disclosed nameplate capacity, power distribution architecture, or intended workload mix.

Without published megawatt figures, this campus cannot be assessed against other data center infrastructure in the state. New York has 31 mapped facilities in this tracking system, but only one other site has disclosed power capacity, making the state's total published capacity 3 MW. BlockFusion ranks second by published MW in New York only because the state's published baseline is negligible; this ranking reflects absence of data rather than demonstrated scale.

The lack of published specifications prevents any reading of relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. To matter to grid constraints or accelerator deployment, the operator would need to disclose total power envelope, PUE, IT load allocation, and cooling architecture. Until those figures appear on the operator's own spec page, this campus remains mapped but opaque.
